sanity_expectations: lambda >= 0 everywhere over the sampled domain (force of infection is non-negative)
lambda finite and real (no blow-up; denominators 1+h*c*p and Hill terms are strictly positive)
lambda increases with c and with p at low c*p, then saturates in c*p due to contact-handling term
at high c, p, and I_signal the new fatigue-reactivation term raises lambda above the parent-equation prediction
lambda decreases as b increases (behavioral suppression of the baseline channel)
excitation_report: sigma=0.01, k=5 (sobol, 512 samples, 4D). Per-term RMS multiples of sigma: term1 baseline-transmission beta0*c*p*exp(-b*p)/(1+h*c*p) = 20.3x; term2 residual/compliance channel = 7.7x; term3 new fatigue-reactivation channel = 5.5x. NEW term (E - parent) peak effect 0.190 = 19.0x sigma, strongest at c~29.3, p~0.28, I_signal~8.7, b~3.1 (high contact, high prevalence, high awareness — where the crowding gate and fatigue erosion both engage). No weak terms; all visible above noise.

rationale: Structure from analyze_expression: no derivatives, no integral kernels, target lambda on the LHS and explicitly solvable => static explicit algebraic response, matching the 'algebraic response under varying sampled conditions' phenomenon (integrator evaluate_explicit). Roles: lambda is the determined output; c, p, I_signal, b are the sampling axes (c, p, and behavioral-response strength b are named as functional arguments in the phenomenon, and I_signal must vary to excite the awareness-driven compliance and fatigue channels); all remaining symbols are fixed background parameters. Parameter magnitudes chosen for epidemiological plausibility (transmission probs ~0.2-0.3, prevalence up to 0.3, Hill exponents ~2, compliance 0.7) and to make the contact-handling saturation (h*c*p ~ O(1-5)) and fatigue reactivation engage within the domain. auto_balance converged with no rescaling (changed={}); excitation_check confirms all three additive terms reach >=5*sigma and the new fatigue term peaks at 19x sigma in the high-contact/high-prevalence/high-awareness corner.

scenario_text: During an outbreak, the effective per-contact transmission is reduced by behavioral interventions whose intensity depends on the currently observed infection level. Researchers measure the instantaneous force of infection as a function of contact rate, current prevalence, and the strength of behavioral response. This is treated as an algebraic response under varying sampled conditions rather than a time integration. Population size and susceptibility are fixed background quantities.
